tasks.short: Initiate, facilitate, and moderate classroom discussions in the economics seminar.

steps.what: Read the seminar notes before this economics class
Initiate classroom discussions with one economics question
facilitate turns so each student can answer the question
moderate the discussion when a claim or a student is shut out

tasks.design: She still initiates the discussion with one economics question, facilitates turns, and moderates when a claim or a student is shut out. The talk stays in the room. No attendance note and no second entry are part of this task, so none of that time is removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The discussion is spoken and changes with who is in the room. A prepared question does not take the next turn.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing now takes the seminar. Tools that mark an essay do not initiate, facilitate, or moderate this discussion.
tasks.still_hard: A student can be shut out in one sentence, and only she hears the tone. Inferring emotions to run the room is prohibited.
tasks.human_edge: She hears when a claim is wrong and when a student has stopped speaking, and she opens the next turn.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still initiates, facilitates, and moderates the classroom discussion.

reach.task: Run the seminar when she is away
reach.learn: Stop a claim without taking the discussion over

evidence.claim: The discussion is live in the room. She starts it, gives turns, and steps in when a student is shut out.
Emotion inference in education is prohibited.

assumptions: Initiating the question, facilitating turns, and moderating when someone is shut out are the work she does in the room today. Each stays at full time because the design does not change that talk.
Reading the seminar notes is the short start. Opening with one question is next. Giving turns is the long middle of the seminar. Stepping in when a student is shut out is the rest.
There is no second entry into another system in this task, and she does not file an attendance note as part of it, so no filing time is removed.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
Essays, exams, and grades are other tasks. They are outside this discussion.
If a teaching assistant already runs the seminar, that time is not hers. The saving on this task is still zero.
unknowns: Whether a teaching assistant already runs some of these seminars.
Whether she writes seminar notes for every class or only for a new topic.
research_questions: Does she open written seminar notes before every class, or only when the topic is new?

already_counted.description: She still reads the notes, opens the discussion, gives turns, and moderates when a student is shut out.

incremental.description: No list or template is kept for the seminar. Upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still runs the seminar. A class another teacher already leads is not her time, and no step here is removed. The high stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise undergraduate or graduate teaching, internship, and research work in person.

steps.what: Read the undergraduate or graduate research or internship update
Meet the student and hear what blocked the work
Judge whether the teaching or research work meets the standard
outputs: whether the work meets the standard

steps.what: Supervise the next piece of work and say what must change
inputs: whether the work meets the standard

tasks.design: She still reads the update, meets the student, judges whether the teaching or research work meets the standard, and says what must change. Research supervision stays with her. No status entry is filed from this meeting, so no filing time is removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The standard for this student's work depends on the project and on what blocked them. A checklist does not hear that.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing now replaces the meeting. Research supervision stays with her.
tasks.still_hard: She has to say the work is not yet good enough, including when that affects a placement or a thesis.
tasks.human_edge: She knows the project and can tell a careful result from one that only looks finished.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still supervises the teaching, internship, and research work in the meeting.

reach.task: Hear the placement before her meeting
reach.learn: Which placement problems she still has to judge herself

evidence.claim: She reads the student's update, hears what blocked the work, and says whether the teaching or research work meets the standard.
A grade set solely by a model is restricted, and systematic automated evaluation needs a data-protection assessment. This supervision meeting is not that decision.

assumptions: Reading the update, hearing what blocked the work, judging the standard, and saying what must change are the supervision she does today. Each stays at full time.
Reading the update is shorter than the meeting. Hearing the blockage is the next block. Judging the standard is the longest part. Saying what must change is the close.
She does not file a status entry as part of this meeting, so no filing time is removed.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
Grading a paper and refereeing a grant are other tasks. They are outside this meeting.
If the internship coordinator already judged the placement, that time is not hers. The saving on this task is still zero.
unknowns: Whether the internship coordinator already judges the placement before her meeting.
Whether the update arrives as a document or only as speech in the meeting.
research_questions: What share of this supervision is a placement the coordinator already reviewed?

already_counted.description: She still reads the update, hears the blockage, judges the standard, and says what must change.

incremental.description: No list or template is kept for these meetings. Upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still holds the supervision meeting. If the internship coordinator already judged the placement, that time is not hers, and this task still has nothing removed. The high stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain regularly scheduled office hours to advise and assist students.

steps.what: Maintain regularly scheduled office hours by being there
Hear the question the student brings to the hour
advise and assist students on the economics problem they brought
Tell the student what to try before the next class

tasks.design: She still keeps the scheduled hour, hears the question, advises and assists on the problem the student brought, and says what to try next. Advising stays with her. She does not re-enter the hour anywhere else in this task, so no second entry is removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The student brings a problem she has not seen. Being in the room is the task.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing now holds the hour. Advising stays with her.
tasks.still_hard: The useful next step depends on what the student already tried, which she hears only in the hour.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a stuck method from a wrong idea and say the next try in that moment.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still keeps the office hour and advises the student who comes.

reach.task: Sit the hour only when she asks
reach.learn: Which questions she still wants to hear herself

evidence.claim: Office hours are a scheduled presence. She hears the question the student brings and says what to try next.
Inferring a student's emotions during the hour is prohibited.

assumptions: Being there, hearing the question, advising on the problem, and saying what to try next are the hour she keeps today. Each stays at full time.
Being there includes the quiet time between students. Hearing the question is next. Advising on the problem they brought is most of the hour. Saying what to try next is the close.
She does not book the hour again inside this task, so no second entry is removed.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
Curriculum planning and career letters are other tasks. They are outside this hour.
If a colleague already sits this hour, that time is not hers. The saving on this task is still zero.
unknowns: Whether students book the hour or walk in.
Whether she posts the hour herself or a coordinator already did.
research_questions: Do students arrive with a written question or only a spoken one?

already_counted.description: She still keeps the hour, hears the question, advises, and says what to try next.

incremental.description: No list or template is kept for the hour. Upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still sits the hour. A question a colleague already handled is not this hour, and no step is removed. The high stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise students on academic and vocational curricula and on career issues.

steps.what: Read completed courses for students asking about academic or vocational curricula
Match completed course codes to the required curriculum codes
Judge which unmatched codes matter for this student's goals
outputs: gaps that matter for this student

steps.what: Advise students on career issues once the gaps are clear
inputs: gaps that matter for this student

steps.what: Send the accepted course note to the student

tasks.design: A match on the {LMS} compares completed course codes with the required curriculum codes and names the codes that do not line up. She still judges which gaps matter, advises the student on career issues, and writes the course note. She sends that note from {EMAIL} only after she has accepted it, and that send stays her work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Required codes and completed codes sit on the same screen, but she still walks them by eye, and exemptions live in letters.
tasks.enabler_now: Both sets are already codes on the {LMS}, so a match can name the codes that do not line up. She still decides which gaps matter.
tasks.still_hard: A renamed course, a foreign course, or an exemption in a letter will not match a current code.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which gap blocks this student and which one a letter already covers.
tasks.altitude: The code comparison is shorter. She still chooses the path, still advises on career issues, and still sends any note. She gains no right to waive a requirement.

reach.task: Name the current code for a renamed or foreign course
reach.learn: Which old code she must type before the match

evidence.claim: Before a curriculum talk she compares completed course codes with the required codes on the study-progress screen.
A grade set solely by automated processing is restricted. Matching course codes is not that decision; she still chooses the path.

assumptions: Today she compares completed course codes with the required curriculum codes by eye on the study-progress screen before the talk. She produces the unmatched codes herself by that comparison. That comparison is the work removed.
The meeting, the path choice, and the email stay at full time. Sending the accepted course note is not removed work, because the note still goes to the student.
The programme office already publishes requirement codes. The student office already posts completions. Neither is new labour on this task.
When a renamed course has no current code, she types the old code so the match can see it. That typing is the one extra hour per 100 hours of this task.
She still chooses the path and still writes any note. She gains no right to waive a requirement.

Reading both code sets is the start. The eye comparison is a large part of the preparation before the student sits down. Judging which gaps matter and advising on career issues are the meeting. Sending the note is the short close.
unknowns: Whether this programme states requirements as course codes or only as prose.
Whether the student already named the remaining courses before the meeting.
Whether a renamed-course alias is already on the programme list.
research_questions: How often are curriculum requirements stated as course codes rather than prose?

already_counted.description: She still reads both code sets, judges which gaps matter, advises on career issues, and sends the note.

incremental.description: When a renamed course has no current code, she types the old code so the match can see it.

approvals.approved_version: the course note she accepted in s4, including any wording she rewrote there

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low is zero when the student already listed the remaining codes, or the programme states requirements only in prose. The high is 12 when most requirements are codes and she still rechecks exemptions in the meeting, after the hour for a renamed course.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: More of the week stays in the seminar and the supervision meetings. The code comparison is a shorter start to a curriculum talk. She gains no right to set a grade, waive a requirement, or sanction fraud.
skills_to_grow: Read a gap list that missed an exemption in a letter.
Stop a seminar claim without taking the discussion over.
Tell a placement student the work is not yet good enough.
role.ambitious_version: A student arrives having already compared their completed codes with the required codes, and books her only for the path choice. She still teaches the seminar and still signs nothing the programme office must sign.
